correctness.rationale: Every initial-color cohort on a shore remains synchronized and never splits; truncation of its cardinality at two exactly preserves threshold-two neighbor counts under any future mergers. This proves a universal 676-representative quotient. An exhaustive full-state period search on these representatives yields preperiod at most three and periods 1,3,4, with a complete histogram. For each period, formal integer-polynomial sums over the 676 representative pairs are proved equal coefficient by coefficient to the asserted closed four-variable formulas. Exponential generating-function coefficient extraction gives B_3 and B_4 for every integer a,b>=2. An independent labelled vertex-level checker exhausts 1,185,921 states across 25 size pairs, corroborating the quotient but not substituting for the all-size proof. All boundary cases 2,3,4,5,6 and the sharp preperiod witness were checked; the period existence claims follow from positivity of H,J,K,L,U.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete dynamical classification of the eventual-period basin sizes, sharp first-periodic-entry cutoff, and primitive cycles on an infinite two-parameter graph family. The period-three existence gap (with one shore of size six, opposite shore sizes two or three and six onward support 3-cycles, but four and five do not) is a motivated nonmonotone structural boundary. The exact generating-polynomial certificate explains the asymptotic concentration of random starts into period-three attraction as both shores grow; this is not a routine rewrite of any inspected threshold-one or GHM theorem.
